title: Hosted GPU capacity surge mitigation retrospective and long-tail hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2025-02-09 we observed a rapid hosted API traffic surge that caused sustained queue growth on several GPU pools in us-east-1. Autoscaling hit rate limits and our admission control started dropping requests which manifested as elevated 429s and increased latency for high-throughput customers. This ticket captures follow-ups from the incident retro and defines prioritized, owner-assigned remediation and medium-term hardening work.
action_items: ENG-24621: Implement per-pool soft admission with token-bucket smoothing (owner: Marcus Nguyen) - PoC by 2025-02-26
ENG-24622: Add per-tenant circuit breakers with exponential backoff to avoid single-tenant amplification (owner: Leila Gomez) - rollout by 2025-03-05
ENG-24623: Provision a warm GPU node pool with instant-burst capacity (owner: Kai Matsuo) - infra plan by 2025-02-20
ENG-24624: Improve autoscaler rate-limit backoff and faster scale-up path for host pools (owner: Priya Shah) - merge target 2025-02-28
ENG-24625: Instrument live queue length and KV cache hit-rate in Console with alert thresholds and runbook links (owner: Tom Walker) - dashboard by 2025-02-21
ENG-24626: Add adaptive request prioritization based on SLA tier and recent token usage (owner: Sofia Alvarez) - spec complete 2025-02-23
ENG-24627: Create a synthetic load test harness that replays measured client burst patterns for pre-deploy verification (owner: QA Team) - initial runs by 2025-02-24
ENG-24628: Audit and tighten rate-limit policies exposed to hosted API clients; add guidance in docs for high-throughput users (owner: Developer Experience) - publish 2025-02-22
ENG-24629: Post-incident blameless customer outreach and compensation plan drafted (owner: Customer Success) - send by 2025-02-18
decisions: Prefer soft admission and smoothing over aggressive early shedding to avoid oscillation between throttling and autoscaler churn.
Warm node pool preferred to cold-starting GPUs for bursty workloads; will be configurable per-region and per-customer tier.
Introduce tenant-level circuit breakers rather than global queue cutoffs to avoid single-customer blast radius.
Short-term mitigation (2-week) prioritized instrumentation and smaller behavioral changes; medium-term (quarter) changes include autoscaler and admission redesign.
Keep default hosted API rate-limits conservative while surfacing a clear path to reserved capacity (Dedicated) for heavy users.
comments: 2025-02-09 04:12 - Incident detected: sustained queue increase in us-east-1 GPU pool. Notified on-call.
2025-02-09 04:27 - Quick mitigation: lowered per-request concurrency per worker and enabled emergency queue shedding for non-SLA routes. Reduced immediate latency but caused 429s for some customers.
2025-02-09 06:00 - Autoscaler logs show throttled API to cloud provider rate limits; scale-up delayed ~6 minutes due to provisioning churn.

2025-02-10 10:34 - Retro: identified three contributing factors: bursty client behavior that bypassed recommended rate-limits, autoscaler slow path for large-scale adds, and coarse global shedding policy.
2025-02-12 09:20 - Engineering triage: agreed on short-term instrument+soft-admit approach to reduce oscillation and implement warm pool as medium-term capacity buffer.
2025-02-17 16:45 - Design review: prioritization rules discussed; decided to use SLA tier + recent token rate as primary input; edge cases for function calls and streaming considered.
2025-02-18 11:02 - Customer Success confirmed 4 customers experienced degraded SLA; compensation plan drafted and aligned with legal.
2025-02-19 08:10 - This ticket created to track the consolidated action items and owners. Linking infra and runtime PRs for coordination.
